# Condylomata Acuminata (Genital Warts)

**Authors:** Stephen W. Leslie, Hussain Sajjad, Sandeep Kumar

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Genital warts (condyloma acuminata) are the clinical manifestations of a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by some types of human papillomavirus (HPV). Genital warts are a recognized symptom of genital HPV infections. About 90% of those exposed who contract HPV will not develop genital warts, and only about 10% who are infected will transmit the virus. Two types, HPV types 6 and 11, cause 90% of all genital warts. The American Cancer Society reports that there are over 200 different known types of HPV, but only 14 are considered high-risk for possible malignant transformation, including anal, cervical, oropharyngeal, and penile cancers. Human papillomavirus is spread through direct skin-to-skin contact with an infected individual, usually during sex. While some types of HPV cause cervical and anal cancer, these are not the same viral types that cause genital warts (see Image. Condylomata Acuminata). Infection with different HPV types at the same time is also possible.
